raw_response_text:
{
  "project_id": "P-MNG-ThirdEnergySector",
  "risks": [
    {
      "risk_id": "R01",
      "description": "Construction may be delayed if the 220 kV line is not completed before the winter season, forcing work to pause until the next construction window.",
      "category": "schedule",
      "likelihood": 4,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Advance procurement and mobilization to start civil works early; develop a detailed seasonal work plan and secure winter‑grade materials to allow limited winter construction.",
      "evidence": "If it cannot be completed before winter, the Project will have more delays with waiting for the next construction season."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R02",
      "description": "Limited local capacity to supply 220 kV poles, conductors and related equipment may cause supply gaps and quality issues.",
      "category": "technical",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 3,
      "mitigation": "Engage qualified international suppliers early, include quality‑control clauses in contracts, and provide technical assistance to develop local fabricators.",
      "evidence": "no local company who can produce metal poles and conductors meeting the standards for 220kV lines and equipment for substations."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R03",
      "description": "New PMO staff may lack experience with World Bank fiduciary procedures, risking improper use of loan proceeds.",
      "category": "financial",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Recruit experienced financial officers, conduct intensive FM training, and implement a robust FMM with Bank oversight during the first year.",
      "evidence": "PMO is not yet in place and no financial management staff has been appointed; lack of experience may cause FM risks."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R04",
      "description": "Budget overruns could arise from heavy reliance on imported construction materials and a 40% unqualified material rate in the local market.",
      "category": "financial",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Implement strict material quality assurance, pre‑qualify suppliers, and include contingency buffers in the budget for price escalations.",
      "evidence": "75‑80% of construction materials are sourced from outside; 40% of construction materials were found unqualified in the local market."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R05",
      "description": "Bird collisions and avian biodiversity impacts may occur despite route realignment, affecting environmental compliance.",
      "category": "environmental",
      "likelihood": 2,
      "impact": 3,
      "mitigation": "Install flight diverters, conduct regular avian monitoring, and adapt tower designs to minimize collision risk.",
      "evidence": "Transmission lines in Mongolia often involve bird collision and other biodiversity issues; BMP addresses potential impacts on avifauna."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R06",
      "description": "Construction activities could temporarily restrict herders' access to pasture and water, leading to community grievances.",
      "category": "stakeholder",
      "likelihood": 2,
      "impact": 2,
      "mitigation": "Develop a community liaison plan, schedule works to avoid peak grazing periods, and provide alternative water points where needed.",
      "evidence": "temporary restriction of access to resources by local herders (for example, pasture, wells, etc.)"
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R07",
      "description": "Extreme weather (high winds, snow, earthquakes, floods) may damage transmission towers, compromising grid reliability.",
      "category": "environmental",
      "likelihood": 2,
      "impact": 3,
      "mitigation": "Apply enhanced engineering standards for wind loading, snow, freezing, seismic and flood resistance in tower design and conduct periodic inspections.",
      "evidence": "enhanced engineering and design standards that consider weather and natural hazards in the tower structures design."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R08",
      "description": "Changes in government officials after elections could disrupt project continuity and decision‑making.",
      "category": "political_regulatory",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 3,
      "mitigation": "Maintain regular briefings with incoming officials, secure formal commitments in the PSC charter, and document implementation milestones.",
      "evidence": "Potential changes in Government officials involved in project activities due to election cycle."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R09",
      "description": "Current electricity tariffs are below cost, risking utility financial deficits that may affect loan repayment and project sustainability.",
      "category": "financial",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Support tariff reform studies, implement cost‑reflective pricing mechanisms, and establish a reserve fund to cover short‑term deficits.",
      "evidence": "current electricity price is below the cost of service causing financial difficulties for sector utilities; deficit could reach 36% of system costs."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R10",
      "description": "Private investors may develop less renewable capacity than expected, reducing the project's private‑capital‑enabling impact.",
      "category": "external",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 3,
      "mitigation": "Offer risk‑mitigation instruments (e.g., guarantees), streamline curtailment rules, and provide market‑information support to attract investors.",
      "evidence": "only 100 MW will be developed by private investors, translating to US$110 million in private capital enabling."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R11",
      "description": "Perceived corruption and high‑level official interference in procurement could cause delays and reputational risk.",
      "category": "stakeholder",
      "likelihood": 2,
      "impact": 3,
      "mitigation": "Adopt transparent e‑GP procurement, enforce conflict‑of‑interest policies, and involve independent observers in evaluation committees.",
      "evidence": "High level of corruption perception. Interference of the high-level officials in procurement decision making which leads to delays."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R12",
      "description": "Administrative and technical capacity constraints of implementing agencies may lead to implementation delays.",
      "category": "organizational",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 3,
      "mitigation": "Establish the PMO early, provide targeted capacity‑building workshops, and embed an Owner’s Engineer to fill expertise gaps.",
      "evidence": "previous infrastructure projects in Mongolia have experienced implementation delays due to the administrative and technical capacity constraints of the implementing agencies."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R13",
      "description": "The existing single‑circuit Baganuur‑Choir line is a bottleneck, risking supply outages until the new line is operational.",
      "category": "technical",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Prioritize rapid construction of the double‑circuit line and implement interim load‑shedding protocols to manage outages.",
      "evidence": "Baganuur‑Choir corridor remains as a bottleneck for power transmission because it lacks redundancy with only a single circuit 220kV line."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R14",
      "description": "Pandemic‑related border closures could disrupt import of construction materials, inflating costs and causing schedule slips.",
      "category": "external",
      "likelihood": 2,
      "impact": 3,
      "mitigation": "Maintain buffer stocks of critical materials, diversify supplier base, and monitor global logistics to adjust procurement timelines.",
      "evidence": "any potential risks related to the pandemic or border closures could have a significant impact on the sector, potentially leading to increased costs and delays."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R15",
      "description": "If audit quality is poor or findings are not acted upon, financial mismanagement may go undetected.",
      "category": "financial",
      "likelihood": 2,
      "impact": 3,
      "mitigation": "Engage a reputable external auditor, enforce timely implementation of audit recommendations, and conduct periodic internal audits.",
      "evidence": "Unqualified auditors may audit the project implementation. Poor follow‑up on audit findings."
    }
  ]
}

risks.description: Construction may be delayed if the 220 kV line is not completed before the winter season, forcing work to pause until the next construction window.
risks.mitigation: Advance procurement and mobilization to start civil works early; develop a detailed seasonal work plan and secure winter‑grade materials to allow limited winter construction.
risks.evidence: If it cannot be completed before winter, the Project will have more delays with waiting for the next construction season.

risks.description: Limited local capacity to supply 220 kV poles, conductors and related equipment may cause supply gaps and quality issues.
risks.mitigation: Engage qualified international suppliers early, include quality‑control clauses in contracts, and provide technical assistance to develop local fabricators.
risks.evidence: no local company who can produce metal poles and conductors meeting the standards for 220kV lines and equipment for substations.

risks.description: New PMO staff may lack experience with World Bank fiduciary procedures, risking improper use of loan proceeds.
risks.mitigation: Recruit experienced financial officers, conduct intensive FM training, and implement a robust FMM with Bank oversight during the first year.
risks.evidence: PMO is not yet in place and no financial management staff has been appointed; lack of experience may cause FM risks.

risks.description: Budget overruns could arise from heavy reliance on imported construction materials and a 40% unqualified material rate in the local market.
risks.mitigation: Implement strict material quality assurance, pre‑qualify suppliers, and include contingency buffers in the budget for price escalations.
risks.evidence: 75‑80% of construction materials are sourced from outside; 40% of construction materials were found unqualified in the local market.

risks.description: Bird collisions and avian biodiversity impacts may occur despite route realignment, affecting environmental compliance.
risks.mitigation: Install flight diverters, conduct regular avian monitoring, and adapt tower designs to minimize collision risk.
risks.evidence: Transmission lines in Mongolia often involve bird collision and other biodiversity issues; BMP addresses potential impacts on avifauna.

risks.description: Construction activities could temporarily restrict herders' access to pasture and water, leading to community grievances.
risks.mitigation: Develop a community liaison plan, schedule works to avoid peak grazing periods, and provide alternative water points where needed.
risks.evidence: temporary restriction of access to resources by local herders (for example, pasture, wells, etc.)

risks.description: Extreme weather (high winds, snow, earthquakes, floods) may damage transmission towers, compromising grid reliability.
risks.mitigation: Apply enhanced engineering standards for wind loading, snow, freezing, seismic and flood resistance in tower design and conduct periodic inspections.
risks.evidence: enhanced engineering and design standards that consider weather and natural hazards in the tower structures design.

risks.description: Changes in government officials after elections could disrupt project continuity and decision‑making.
risks.mitigation: Maintain regular briefings with incoming officials, secure formal commitments in the PSC charter, and document implementation milestones.
risks.evidence: Potential changes in Government officials involved in project activities due to election cycle.

risks.description: Current electricity tariffs are below cost, risking utility financial deficits that may affect loan repayment and project sustainability.
risks.mitigation: Support tariff reform studies, implement cost‑reflective pricing mechanisms, and establish a reserve fund to cover short‑term deficits.
risks.evidence: current electricity price is below the cost of service causing financial difficulties for sector utilities; deficit could reach 36% of system costs.

risks.description: Private investors may develop less renewable capacity than expected, reducing the project's private‑capital‑enabling impact.
risks.mitigation: Offer risk‑mitigation instruments (e.g., guarantees), streamline curtailment rules, and provide market‑information support to attract investors.
risks.evidence: only 100 MW will be developed by private investors, translating to US$110 million in private capital enabling.

risks.description: Perceived corruption and high‑level official interference in procurement could cause delays and reputational risk.
risks.mitigation: Adopt transparent e‑GP procurement, enforce conflict‑of‑interest policies, and involve independent observers in evaluation committees.
risks.evidence: High level of corruption perception. Interference of the high-level officials in procurement decision making which leads to delays.

risks.description: Administrative and technical capacity constraints of implementing agencies may lead to implementation delays.
risks.mitigation: Establish the PMO early, provide targeted capacity‑building workshops, and embed an Owner’s Engineer to fill expertise gaps.
risks.evidence: previous infrastructure projects in Mongolia have experienced implementation delays due to the administrative and technical capacity constraints of the implementing agencies.

risks.description: The existing single‑circuit Baganuur‑Choir line is a bottleneck, risking supply outages until the new line is operational.
risks.mitigation: Prioritize rapid construction of the double‑circuit line and implement interim load‑shedding protocols to manage outages.
risks.evidence: Baganuur‑Choir corridor remains as a bottleneck for power transmission because it lacks redundancy with only a single circuit 220kV line.

risks.description: Pandemic‑related border closures could disrupt import of construction materials, inflating costs and causing schedule slips.
risks.mitigation: Maintain buffer stocks of critical materials, diversify supplier base, and monitor global logistics to adjust procurement timelines.
risks.evidence: any potential risks related to the pandemic or border closures could have a significant impact on the sector, potentially leading to increased costs and delays.

risks.description: If audit quality is poor or findings are not acted upon, financial mismanagement may go undetected.
risks.mitigation: Engage a reputable external auditor, enforce timely implementation of audit recommendations, and conduct periodic internal audits.
risks.evidence: Unqualified auditors may audit the project implementation. Poor follow‑up on audit findings.
